scope: Current PS4 and GTA 5 dashboards in local CUA preview

selectedFileMime.finding: A valid exact BIN was rejected solely because browser File.type metadata was neither empty nor application/octet-stream.
selectedFileMime.change: File identity now uses its BIN filename, exact declared and actual byte length, non-ELF magic check and exact SHA-256. Browser MIME metadata does not determine payload identity. Pairing, same-origin, platform, firmware, game-version and approved loader checks remain in place.

tests.wrongBytes: For every MIME variation, changed bytes with the same declared length fail checksum before another POST. Existing filename, length, ELF, read-timeout and prerequisite rejection coverage still passes.
tests.transport: Authored four-byte fixture and mocked fetch only; no real console or downloaded payload was used.

phoneOverflow.priorEvidence: docs/qa/host-repository-browser.json recorded document clientWidth 430 and scrollWidth 431.
phoneOverflow.method: Read-only DOM and computed-layout measurements in CUA on a loopback preview of authored site pages. Exact 430 by 900 viewport with ArabicGuy version chooser open and firmware 9.00 selected; no console address configured.
phoneOverflow.conclusion: The prior one-pixel overflow cannot be assigned a precise CSS cause from the saved evidence. Current connection and popup content fit the viewport, so no speculative CSS change was made.

remainingScope.newUiImprovementOwnedByRoot: Expose the exact expected selected filename, byte size and SHA-256 in collapsed file details so the existing exact-file instructions are reviewable before selection.
remainingScope.sourceReviewOwnedByOtherAgents: Source-backed older-firmware menu variants and a stable original FTP release are separate catalogue tasks; this audit did not infer new compatibility.
limitations: No physical console contacted, exploit page opened, payload executed or hardware compatibility asserted.
Browser file metadata variations are authored fixtures; no claim is made that every browser or OS assigns those specific MIME values automatically.
No existing download, archived version or unrelated shared change was removed.
